_note: Hand-curated reference index for non-event entities: peer reports, government programs, theoretical-physics frameworks, facilities, and sensor classes. Events in events.json carry crossRefs[] pointing into this file by id. Update HOW-CAN-I-HELP.md to contribute additions.

reports.title: The Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research
reports.summary: AAWSA-commissioned DIRD surveying claimed and observed coupling between superconductors and the gravitational field — Podkletnov-type rotating-disc experiments, Heim-Dröscher hyperspace coupling, and asymmetric gravitomagnetic effects. Sets the theoretical frame in which DoE/Pantex anomalous sensor returns are interpreted.

reports.title: Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions
reports.summary: Companion AAWSA DIRD on metric-engineering and Alcubierre-class propulsion. Often co-cited with the superconductor paper as the theoretical envelope for the AAWSA programme.

programs.name: AAWSA
programs.fullName: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program
programs.summary: DIA-funded successor to AAWSAP; produced ~38 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents on advanced propulsion, materials science, and theoretical-physics frameworks for anomalous aerospace phenomena.

programs.name: AARO
programs.summary: Current DoD office of record for UAP investigation, sensor-data review, and historical-record review. Successor to AOIMSG / UAPTF.

frameworks.title: Superconductor-mediated gravitomagnetic coupling
frameworks.discipline: theoretical physics — general relativity / condensed matter
frameworks.summary: Hypothesis class in which rotating or oscillating superconductors exhibit anomalous coupling to the gravitational field (Podkletnov 1992, Tajmar 2006). Used by DIA AAWSA as the candidate framework for anomalous radar/imaging returns at nuclear-research sites.

frameworks.title: Nuclear-site UAP clustering
frameworks.summary: Documented pattern in which UAP sightings cluster at nuclear-weapons assembly, storage, and research facilities (Hastings 2008, Salas 2010). Pantex, Sandia, Los Alamos, and Oak Ridge are all primary sites in the open-archive record.

facilities.name: Pantex Plant
facilities.summary: Only US facility that assembles, disassembles, and modifies nuclear weapons. Co-located with the Pantex Wildlife Refuge. Ground Surveillance Radar coverage of the perimeter is the data source for DOE-UAP-D001.

facilities.name: Sandia National Laboratories
facilities.summary: DoE weapons-research lab adjacent to Kirtland AFB. Hosts radar-cross-section ranges and the original Pantex image-enhancement work referenced in DOE-UAP-D001.

facilities.name: Los Alamos National Laboratory
facilities.summary: Manhattan Project laboratory, ongoing weapons-design and applied-physics research. James L. Tuck (DOE-UAP-D002 correspondent) was a staff physicist here.

facilities.name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory
facilities.summary: Manhattan Project enrichment site. Section 2 of FBI-62HQ-83894 documents repeated 1947–1950 UAP sightings over Oak Ridge by AEC security and military police.

sensors.name: Ground Surveillance Radar Tower
sensors.summary: Static-tower L/S-band perimeter radar used at nuclear-weapons sites. Cross-references the imagery in DOE-UAP-D001 to a primary sensor of record.

sensors.name: LP/OP visual observation
sensors.summary: Listening-post / observation-post sentinel sighting protocol. The primary sensor for the USPER-2025 helicopter encounter.

sensors.name: FLIR targeting-pod IR
sensors.summary: Forward-looking infrared targeting pod (ATFLIR / Sniper-XR) — the primary instrument behind the Nimitz Tic-Tac and Gimbal videos.
